arxiv-2109-02818.title: List-decodable Codes and Covering Codes
arxiv-2109-02818.creator: Hao Chen
arxiv-2109-02818.description: Abstract The list-decodable code has been an active topic in theoretical computer science since the seminal papers of M. Sudan and V. Guruswami in 1997-1998. There are general results about the list-decodability to the Johnson radius and the list-decoding capacity theorem. However few results about general constraints on rates, list-decodable radius and list sizes for list-decodable codes have been obtained.

arxiv-2309-13946.title: Observational constraints on interactions between dark energy and dark matter with momentum and energy transfers
arxiv-2309-13946.creator: Xiaolin Liu 1,5 , Shinji Tsujikawa 2 , Kiyotomo Ichiki 3,4,5
arxiv-2309-13946.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Xiaolin Liu 1,5 , Shinji Tsujikawa 2 , Kiyotomo Ichiki 3,4,5. We place observational constraints on a dark energy (DE) model in which a quintessence scalar field ϕ \phi is coupled to dark matter (DM) through momentum and energy exchanges.

arxiv-2402-05444.title: Refined TSSOS Thanks:
arxiv-2402-05444.creator: Daria Shaydurova, Volker Kaibel, Sebastian Sager
arxiv-2402-05444.description: Abstract The moment-sum of squares hierarchy by Lasserre has become an established technique for solving polynomial optimization problems. It provides a monotonically increasing series of tight bounds, but has well-known scalability limitations. For structured optimization problems, the term-sparsity SOS (TSSOS) approach scales much better due to block-diagonal matrices, obtained by completing the connected components of adjacency graphs.

arxiv-2405-12616.title: Towards Using Fast Embedded Model Predictive Control for Human-Aware Predictive Robot Navigation
arxiv-2405-12616.creator: Till Hielscher, Lukas Heuer, Frederik Wulle, Luigi Palmieri
arxiv-2405-12616.description: Abstract Predictive planning is a key capability for robots to efficiently and safely navigate populated environments. Particularly in densely crowded scenes, with uncertain human motion predictions, predictive path planning, and control can become expensive to compute in real time due to the curse of dimensionality.

arxiv-2407-03340.title: A Multi-Modal Explainability Approach for Human-Aware Robots in Multi-Party Conversation
arxiv-2407-03340.creator: Iveta Bečková *, Štefan Pócoš *, Giulia Belgiovine, Marco Matarese, Omar Eldardeer, Alessandra Sciutti, Carlo Mazzola
arxiv-2407-03340.description: Abstract The addressee estimation (understanding to whom somebody is talking) is a fundamental task for human activity recognition in multi-party conversation scenarios. Specifically, in the field of human-robot interaction, it becomes even more crucial to enable social robots to participate in such interactive contexts.

arxiv-2512-13760.title: Counting Collatz Numbers
arxiv-2512-13760.creator: Chunlei Liu
arxiv-2512-13760.description: Abstract The counting function π ⁡ ( x ) \pi(x) for the numbers satisfying the Collatz conjecture is studied. A related exponential congruence equation is investigated, yielding a method to construct its solutions from free tuples, and enabling us to obtain the inequality π (x)≥x^0.3227, x→+∞. The historical record is 0.84.

pmc-10532762.title: Mitochondrial DNA Copy Number Drives the Penetrance of Acute Intermittent Porphyria
pmc-10532762.creator: Elena Di Pierro, Miriana Perrone, Milena Franco, Francesca Granata, Lorena Duca, Debora Lattuada, Giacomo De Luca, Giovanna Graziadei, Kezhong Zhang
pmc-10532762.description: No published study has investigated the mitochondrial count in patients suffering from acute intermittent porphyria (AIP). In order to determine whether mitochondrial content can influence the pathogenesis of porphyria, we measured the mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) copy number in the peripheral blood cells of 34 patients and 37 healthy individuals.

pmc-10649071.title: Plastic Evolution Characterization for 304 Stainless Steel by CQN_Chen Model under the Proportional Loading
pmc-10649071.creator: Xiang Gao, Songchen Wang, Zhongming Xu, Jia Zhou, Xinming Wan, Hasib Md Abu Rayhan, Yanshan Lou, Tomasz Trzepieciński
pmc-10649071.description: In this paper, the CQN_Chen function is used to characterize the plastic anisotropic evolution of 304 stainless steel (SS304). The uniaxial tensile tests along different loading directions are conducted to experimentally investigate the anisotropic hardening behavior for SS304. The experimental data indicates that the anisotropy of SS304 is weak.

pmc-11622954.description: BackgroundA brain tumor is the development of abnormal brain cells, some of which may progress to cancer. Early identification of illnesses and development of treatment plans improve patients’ quality of life and life expectancy. Brain tumors are most commonly detected by magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans.

pmc-13206763.title: Long-Term Outcomes of Endoscopic Ultrasound-Guided Gallbladder Drainage for Acute Cholecystitis in Non-Surgical Candidates: A Multicenter Retrospective Study
pmc-13206763.creator: Kei Harada, Kazuya Miyamoto, Kazuyuki Matsumoto, Kosaku Morimoto, Eijiro Ueta, Yutaka Akimoto, Nao Hattori, Taisuke Obata, Ryosuke Sato, Akihiro Matsumi, Hiroyuki Terasawa, Yuki Fujii, Daisuke Uchida, Shigeru Horiguchi, Koichiro Tsutsumi, Motoyuki Otsuka
pmc-13206763.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background/Objectives: Endoscopic ultrasound-guided gallbladder drainage (EUS-GBD) is a minimally invasive alternative for managing acute cholecystitis in patients who are unsuitable for surgery. Although its short-term efficacy is well-established, its long-term outcomes, especially in patients with malignancy-associated cholecystitis, remain unclear. Methods: This multicenter, retrospective study included 139 patients who underwent EUS-GBD with a plastic stent for inoperable acute cholecystitis between January 2010 and October 2023.

pmc-13380072.title: A tree-inspired liquid‐managing scaffold with radial-axial continuity for wound exudate management
pmc-13380072.creator: Xiu-Juan Zhao, Zhao Pan, Lai-Xi Zhao, Zi-Yi Shang, Bao-Ying Li, Meng-Yuan Zhang, Fu-An Yang, Pei-Yang Cheng, Yue-Bo Ma, Si-Ming Li, Rui Xu, Hui-Qin Wen, Liang Dong
pmc-13380072.description: Effective exudate management remains challenging in complex wounds because most dressings rely on local absorption or surface wetting, which readily fail under persistent, heterogeneous, and three-dimensional fluid input. Here, inspired by the radial–axial transport organization of trees, we developed an annealed bioinspired radial–axial convergent scaffold (aBRACS) from regenerated silk fibroin (RSF) via directional ice templating.
